phrases.text: What if ten suns rose at once and scorched the earth?
Chinese legend says they abandoned their usual turns.
Rivers dried, crops burned, and ordinary people suffered under relentless heat.
The earth could not survive ten heavens burning at once.
Hunters, farmers, and animals searched in vain for water or shade.
He was asked to restore balance where power from above had scorched the world below.
He shot down nine suns, one after another.
Each impact dimmed the sky until only the light the world needed remained.
With a single sun moving overhead, crops could grow again.
Water returned to land that had nearly become desert.
The hero did not make the world safe by destroying all power.
He made it livable by leaving enough—and no more.
